senses.gloss: (b. h.; onomatop.) [to sip, absorb, v. שָׂרַף II,] to consume, burn.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 1:4">Pes. I, 4</cite> <he>ושׂוֹרְפִין … שש</he> and the burning (of leavened matter) must take place at the beginning of the sixth hour.

Ab. Zar. 11ᵃ שׂורְפִין על המלכים we do burning at the burial of kings; ומה הן שורפין וכ׳ and what is burnt? Their couch and their objects of service (armor &c.); Tosef. Snh. IV, 3; Tosef. Sabb. VII (VIII), 18; a. fr.—Part. pass. שָׂרוּף; f. שְׂרוּפָה &c.
<cite ref="Niddah 24b:58">Nidd. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>עצמותיו שְׂרוּפִין</he>, v. <cite ref="U02099"><he>שְׁתִיָּה</he> I</cite>; a. e.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 23:1">Num. R. s. 23<sup>6</sup></cite> <he>ונ׳ על שמעל וכ׳</he> and he (Achan) was burned (after being stoned), because he had misappropriated devoted things.
<cite ref="Pesachim 34b:1">Pes. 34ᵇ</cite> <he>יִשָּׂרֵף מיד</he> must be burned at once.
<cite ref="Tosefta Pesachim 5:8">Tosef. ib. V, 8</cite> <he>כשם … אינו נִשְׂרָף וכ׳</he> as the wooden spit (on which the Passover lamb is roasted) does not burn, so the metal spit does not get hot.

<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 12:5">Zeb. XII, 5</cite> <he>בזמן שהם נִשְׂרָפִין כמצותן נשרפין וכ׳</he> when they are burned according to the law concerning them (and not because of a disqualification), they are burned in the ash-house.

<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 12:5">Ib.</cite> a. fr. <he>פרים הנִשְׂרָפִים וכ׳</he> the bullock sacrifices which the law requires to be burned; a. fr.—[Y. Taan. I, 64ᵇ top <he>תשרף</he>, read <he>תשרה</he>, v. <cite ref="U01959"><he>שָׁרָה</he> I</cite>.]
